paraphrase: This teaching frees from saṃsāra even without agnihotra, Sāṃkhya or yoga: the body itself is the sacrifice.

checks.note: E-text 1 located in the e-text; the passage matches the paraphrase.

paraphrase: The sacrifice in the body: food is purified with mantras and offered into the breaths as into the sacrificial fires; the body's fires are named, and the self, intellect, mind and senses are identified with the sacrificer, his wife and the priests; the one who performs this bodily sacrifice is freed from saṃsāra.
notes: Whole-text summary; section numbering and the exact list of correspondences not verified (low).

checks.note: Low-confidence whole-text summary confirmed (Muktikā no. 97, Ātharvaṇīya): khaṇḍa 1 — 'athātaḥ sarvopaniṣatsāraṃ … śārīraṃ yajñaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ … vināpy agnihotreṇa … saṃsāravimuktir bhavati', food purified with mantras and offered 'prāṇāya svāhā …'; khaṇḍa 2 — the bodily fires (sūryāgni, darśanāgni as āhavanīya in the mouth, śārīra/dakṣiṇāgni in the heart, koṣṭhāgni as gārhapatya at the navel); khaṇḍas 3–4 — the questions and answers 'ātmā yajamānaḥ | buddhiḥ patnī | vedā mahartvijaḥ | ahaṅkāro 'dhvaryuḥ | cittaṃ hotā …', ending with liberation. The local edition numbers the last khaṇḍa '3' a second time; four sections in all.

paraphrase: Before eating one sprinkles the food with mantras and offers five oblations to prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna and samāna; the parts of the body are the fire, the priests and the ritual implements.
